llm.summary: The skill’s plant-diagnosis workflow is real, but it silently creates or reuses user identity, sends identity-bearing requests to a cloud service, and stores tokens locally, so it should be reviewed before installation.

dimensions.detail: Uploading local media or passing public URLs to a cloud analysis API is proportionate for this service, but reading workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt, creating workspace data directories, and sending identity fields to remote services expands environmental access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No separate install script or destructive installer was found; the skill relies on Python scripts and declared requirements. Permission needs such as shell execution, file reads/writes, network access, and environment/local identity access are not formally declared in metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest discloses automatic identity association and cloud report lookup, but it frames identity handling as internal and tells the agent not to ask or expose identity values; remote login/registration and token persistence are not clearly surfaced to the user.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common library creates a workspace SQLite database, persists a default user, and may store access tokens, open tokens, and profile fields without a clear retention or cleanup model.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Image/video plant diagnosis and cloud history lookup match the stated purpose, but the implementation also includes silent account creation/login, token handling, local user records, and broad shared API helpers beyond the visible diagnosis task.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the provider receiving plant images/videos or submitted URLs, creating or reusing an automatic identity, querying cloud report history, and storing service tokens in a local workspace database. Avoid sensitive media or internal/private URLs unless the service boundary is acceptable, and review or remove the local data directory if you uninstall.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: Dynamic DAO filter attributes are present and are a robustness/scoping issue, but they are not a code-execution path and are not the main verdict driver.
[LP3] unexpected: The behavior requires shell, network, local file read/write, and local identity access, but no explicit permission metadata was found.
[TP4] unexpected: Cloud history and identity association are partly disclosed, but silent remote login/registration and token persistence materially exceed what a user would infer from plant image diagnosis alone.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The CLI still exposes a generic pet-type parameter, although the configured scene code is plant-specific; this is a quality/scoping mismatch rather than malicious behavior.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Shared account, workspace, and API utility code is bundled with the narrow diagnosis skill; some integration support is understandable, but the scope is broad.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Generic remote write helpers and a user model containing tokens/profile fields are present, and token/profile persistence is not well scoped for the diagnosis purpose.
[SQP-2] expected: Local media upload and URL submission to a cloud API are expected for cloud-based analysis and are mentioned, but users should still treat submitted files and URLs as disclosed to the provider.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Hidden api-key arguments, local identity-file reads, and implicit identity/token transmission are not adequately surfaced as user-controlled security choices.
[E1] unexpected: The phone-login request transmits openId/mobile-style identity data for silent registration/login; this supports the Review verdict because it is under-disclosed for a plant-diagnosis skill.
[P2] expected: The reported hidden character is a zero-width joiner used in an emoji sequence in the notes table, not evidence of concealed evaluator instructions.
[YR4] expected: The metadata/manifest signal appears driven by formatting and rich descriptive text; I did not find artifact-backed prompt poisoning beyond the separate under-disclosed identity behavior.
